result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.has_bridges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if the graph contains any bridge edges. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L19954-L20015){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.has_bridges() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A bridge (cut edge) is an edge whose removal increases the number of connected components. This method is more efficient than `bridges()` when you only need to know if bridges exist, not which edges they are. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if at least one bridge exists, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - more efficient than `len(bridges()) > 0` for large graphs - useful for quick connectivity analysis - returns `False` for complete graphs and cycles ## Examples {.doc-examples} A cycle has no single point of failure, so it has no bridges: ::: {#aa860b34 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_cycle_graph(5) # Returns False (cycles have no bridges) graph.has_bridges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` False ``` ::: ::: A path is the opposite extreme: every edge is a bridge, since there's only one way to get from one end to the other: ::: {#15ec1dc9 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(5) # Returns True (all tree edges are bridges) graph.has_bridges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Attaching a node to a dense component via a single edge introduces exactly one bridge, which this check finds without having to enumerate them: ::: {#e1d068ff .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_cycle_graph(4) graph.add_node(label="isolated") isolated_id = graph.get_id_from_label("isolated") nodes = sorted(graph.get_node_ids()) graph.add_edge(nodes[-2], isolated_id) # Bridge to isolated node # Returns True graph.has_bridges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: :::
